customer_question: If we use an already-certified Controller Subsystem QDID plus a purchased certified Host Subsystem stack, can registration be done purely on paperwork (final product listing only), with no protocol/profile testing (L2CAP, GAP, SPP, etc.)?
question_variants: Do we need L2CAP/GAP/SPP/RFCOMM testing if both Controller and Host Subsystems are already certified?
Is a final-product-only registration possible without further protocol testing when reusing certified subsystem QDIDs?
What additional testing is required for a surface-mount RF module whose antenna feed runs through the product PCB?
Does the host OS (Linux vs Android) matter for RF testing of a certified module?
If our Controller and Host Subsystems are both certified, is any hardware-level RF testing still needed?
actual_issue: The customer planned to combine an already-certified Controller Subsystem QDID with a purchased, certified Host Subsystem stack, and wanted to know whether this combination would avoid protocol/profile-level testing and require only paperwork-based final product registration, given that the RF module is a surface-mount (Type 2AE-style) part whose antenna signal is routed through the product's own PCB pattern.
plain_english_explanation: If both the radio module (Controller Subsystem) and the software stack (Host Subsystem) you're using are already Bluetooth-certified, you generally don't need to redo protocol-level tests like L2CAP/GAP/SPP. However, if the radio module is a surface-mount part where the antenna connection runs through traces on your own circuit board (rather than a fixed antenna on the module itself), the SIG still requires a small RF test to confirm that your board's antenna trace doesn't degrade performance.
consultant_answer: Implementing the certified Host Subsystem as planned means protocol/profile testing (L2CAP, GAP, SPP, etc.) is not required. However, because the Type 2AE-type module is a surface-mount module whose antenna signal is fed through the product's own PCB pattern to the antenna, an RF 2-item test (transmit power and receive sensitivity) is required, performed on a measurement point taken near the feed point, to confirm the design validity of the added antenna pattern. Historically this RF 2-item test has had a 98% pass rate. The test is done at the Japan lab; if the customer sends an RF-test-modified sample plus a simple DUT-mode entry procedure (per the test sample modification guide provided), no on-site witnessing is required. The test itself takes 1 day; registration support takes up to 3 business days, but USD remittance for the registration fee requires about 3 weeks due to internal banking procedures. Because this RF test only exercises the HCI layer and below, the host OS (Linux vs Android) has no bearing on the test.
decision_logic: Certified Controller + certified Host Subsystem normally exempts the product from protocol/profile testing. But if the RF module is surface-mounted and its antenna feed trace runs through the product's own PCB (i.e., the antenna path differs from what was tested during the module's own certification), an RF 2-item test (TX power, RX sensitivity) on the modified feed path is still required to validate that the added PCB antenna pattern doesn't compromise RF performance. This RF-only test is independent of host OS because it only exercises HCI-layer-and-below.
final_recommendation: Plan for an RF 2-item test (TX power, RX sensitivity) at the Japan lab in addition to final product registration, even when both subsystems are certified, because the module's antenna feed runs through the product PCB. No on-site witnessing or special host-OS handling is needed; send a modified RF-test sample with a DUT-mode entry procedure.
risk_if_done_wrong: If the RF 2-item test is skipped on the assumption that 'both subsystems are certified', the antenna pattern added on the product PCB would remain unverified, which could fail to satisfy SIG qualification requirements for the as-built product.
